statement: Let $n\ge0$ and $d\ge1$, $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ nonempty and finite, $j\in P$, and $r_p>0$. Let $T_d=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,\ldots,e_d)$ and give the fibers $\{p\}\times r_pT_d$ their summed ordinary $d$-volume. Suppose $r_p\le r_j+b\cdot(p-j)$ for some $b\in\mathbb R^n$. Then a point maximizing raw mixed halfspace depth over the own fiber $\{j\}\times r_jT_d$ can be chosen at $(j,t\mathbf1)$ with $0<t\le q=r_j/(d+1)$. For $0\le t\le q$, the ordinary raw halfspace depth of $t\mathbf1$ in the own simplex equals $|T_d|(dt)^d$. This amount is also a lower bound for the raw mixed depth at $(j,t\mathbf1)$.
